subsystems.name: Corpus pipeline
subsystems.role: turns statutes into structured, versioned machine-readable text.
parts: XML/HTML schemas such as Akoma Ntoso

subsystems.name: Citation and amendment graph
subsystems.role: models every provision as a node linked to what it references, amends or repeals.

subsystems.name: Norm formalisation layer
subsystems.role: restates selected clauses as rules: who must, may or must not do what, and when.

subsystems.name: Conflict engine
subsystems.role: flags contradictions, duplications and gaps between a draft and existing law.

subsystems.name: Drafting assistant
subsystems.role: proposes clause wording and explains each flag in plain language.
parts: large language model with retrieval augmentation

subsystems.name: Review and audit layer
subsystems.role: keeps a named human accountable and records why each suggestion was accepted or rejected.

buildSteps.title: Digitise the statute book
buildSteps.detail: Convert the body of law into a structured format that records each section, its in-force dates and its amendment history.

buildSteps.title: Build the reference graph
buildSteps.detail: Parse every cross-reference, amendment and repeal so the system knows which provisions depend on which others.

buildSteps.title: Formalise a narrow domain first
buildSteps.detail: Encode obligations, permissions and prohibitions into machine-readable rules for one tractable area, such as benefit eligibility, rather than the whole code.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the retrieval layer
buildSteps.detail: Index the corpus so that when a new clause is drafted, the most relevant existing provisions and precedents are surfaced with citations.

buildSteps.title: Train and prompt the model
buildSteps.detail: Adapt a language model to legislative vocabulary and drafting conventions, testing it on past amendments whose conflicts were found later.

buildSteps.title: Run conflict checks
buildSteps.detail: For each draft clause, combine textual overlap search, semantic contradiction detection and formal satisfiability testing on the formalised rules.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into the drafting editor
buildSteps.detail: Embed the checks in the tool drafters already use, so warnings appear inline with links to the offending provisions.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate against expert review
buildSteps.detail: Measure false positives and false negatives using committees of lawyers, and tune thresholds so alerts stay trustworthy.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with human sign-off
buildSteps.detail: Drafters remain responsible; the system logs every suggestion, its reasoning and the decision taken.

prerequisites.why: some jurisdictions publish structured, dated statute books, but many still publish only PDFs or scanned gazettes.
schemas for rules and norms exist and have been trialled, but coverage of real codes is thin.
finding the relevant few provisions among hundreds of thousands is the core enabling capability.
detecting genuine logical conflict, not just similarity, remains research-grade outside narrow domains.
without agreed tests, claims of accurate conflict detection cannot be verified.

pathway.milestone: AI assistants that summarise, search and suggest wording inside legislative editing tools
pathway.unlocks: faster research and drafting, with alerts limited to obvious duplicate or missing references.

pathway.milestone: rules-as-code pilots in a few narrow domains, with published formalisations
pathway.unlocks: automatic checks of eligibility and procedural logic against the source statutes.

pathway.milestone: graph-backed consistency checking across a whole jurisdiction's in-force law
pathway.unlocks: reviewers see contradictions and orphaned provisions before a bill is tabled.

pathway.milestone: cross-jurisdiction and treaty-level checking, with auditable reasoning
pathway.unlocks: fewer conflicts between national and supranational law — provided accountability stays with human drafters.
